positiveFlows.title: PROJECT ABSTRACT – TEXAS A<(>&<)>M AGRILIFE RESEARCH – ANIMAL HEALTH AND DISEASE RESEARCH PROGRAM  THE PURPOSE OF THESE FUNDS IS TO PROMOTE ANIMAL HEALTH RESEARCH ACROSS THE LAND GRANT UNIVERSITIES AND VETERINARY SCHOOLS.  TEXAS A<(>&<)>M AGRILIFE RESEARCH RECEIVES ANIMAL HEALTH AND DISEASE RESEARCH FUNDS TO ENHANCE AND IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF ANIMALS THROUGH VARIOUS STUDIES. AGRILIFE RESEARCHERS ARE WORKING TO DEVELOP NOVEL VACCINES TO PREVENT REEMERGENCE OF VARIOUS DISEASE, MINIMIZE THE DEVELOPMENT AND EXPORT OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE IN CATTLE, AND UNDERSTANDING TICK POPULATIONS AND THE GENETICS AND VECTORAL CAPACITY, TO NAME A FEW PROJECTS. THEY ALSO WORK TO STUDY THE EFFECTS AND IMPACTS OF ANIMAL HEALTH ON SECURE FOOD SUPPLY PLANS. FUNDS ARE DISTRIBUTED THROUGH AN INTERNAL RFP PROCESS AND THE RESEARCHERS ARE EXPECTED TO PUBLISH THEIR RESULTS AND GROW THEIR RESEARCH PROGRAM THROUGH OTHER EXTERNAL SPONSORED RESEARCH PROJECTS. THE CITIZENS OF TEXAS, THE US AND THE WORLD BENEFIT FROM THE RESEARCH DONE BY THESE RESEARCHERS.

THE USDA DEDICATES FUNDING TO INCREASE ANIMAL HEALTH AND DISEASE RESEARCH ACTIVITIES AT ACCREDITED PUBLIC OR PRIVATE VETERINARY SCHOOLS OR COLLEGES THROUGH THE ANIMAL HEALTH AND DISEASE RESEARCH (AHDR) CAPACITY PROGRAM. THE SCOPE OF THE RESEARCH WHICH MAY BE CONDUCTED WITH AHDR FUNDS IS QUITE BROAD. IT INCLUDES RESEARCH TO PROMOTE THE GENERAL WELFARE THROUGH IMPROVED HEALTH AND PRODUCTIVITY OF DOMESTIC LIVESTOCK, POULTRY, AQUATIC ANIMALS, AND OTHER INCOME-PRODUCING ANIMALS WHICH ARE ESSENTIAL TO THE NATION'S FOOD SUPPLY AND THE WELFARE OF PRODUCERS AND CONSUMERS OF ANIMAL PRODUCTS; TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF HORSES; TO FACILITATE THE EFFECTIVE TREATMENT OF, AND WHERE POSSIBLE, PREVENT, DISEASES IN BOTH DOMESTICATED AND WILD SPECIES WHICH, IF NOT CONTROLLED, WOULD BE DISASTROUS TO THE UNITED STATES ANIMAL INDUSTRIES AND ENDANGER THE NATION'S FOOD SUPPLY; TO MINIMIZE LIVESTOCK AND POULTRY LOSSES DUE TO TRANSPORTATION AND HANDLING; TO PROTECT HUMAN HEALTH THROUGH CONTROL OF ANIMAL DISEASES TRANSMISSIBLE TO HUMANS; TO IMPROVE METHODS OF CONTROLLING REPRODUCTION OF PREDATORS AND OTHER ANIMALS; AND OTHERWISE TO PROMOTE THE GENERAL WELFARE THROUGH EXPANDED PROGRAMS OF RESEARCH AND EXTENSION TO IMPROVE ANIMAL HEALTH.  ANIMAL HEALTH RESEARCH COMPRISES BASIC AND APPLIED STUDIES ON INFECTIOUS AND NONINFECTIOUS AGENTS WHICH IMPAIR THE NORMAL STATE OF THE ANIMAL BODY AND/OR THAT AFFECT THE PERFORMANCE OF VITAL FUNCTIONS. THIS INCLUDES RESEARCH TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF DOMESTIC LIVESTOCK, POULTRY, AQUATIC ANIMALS AND OTHER INCOME-PRODUCING ANIMALS AND TO FACILITATE THE EFFECTIVE PREVENTION OF DISEASES IN BOTH DOMESTICATED AND WILD ANIMALS WHICH, IF NOT CONTROLLED, WOULD ENDANGER THE LIVESTOCK AND POULTRY INDUSTRIES. ALSO INCLUDED IS RESEARCH TO MINIMIZE TRANSPORTATION AND HANDLING LOSSES; MONITOR THE SUITABILITY OF ANIMALS AND ANIMAL PRODUCTS FOR HUMAN USE; PROTECT PUBLIC HEALTH THROUGH CONTROL OF ANIMAL DISEASES TRANSMISSIBLE TO HUMANS AND IMPROVE METHODS OF CONTROLLING THE REPRODUCTION OF PREDATORS.  STUDIES ARE CLASSIFIED AS AHDR IF THE STUDIES RELATE DIRECTLY TO THE HEALTH OF A TARGET LIVESTOCK, POULTRY OR AQUATIC ANIMAL SPECIES AND INCLUDES LABORATORY STUDIES, RESEARCH ON ANIMAL CARE AS IT RELATES TO LIVESTOCK HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, INVESTIGATIONS OF METABOLIC DISEASES AND REPRODUCTIVE DISEASES INCLUDING ENDOCRINE DYSFUNCTIONS SUCH AS ANESTRUS AS WELL AS THE INFRASTRUCTURE AND EQUIPMENT NECESSARY TO COMPLETE THIS RESEARCH. SPECIFIC TO ANIMAL HEALTH AND DISEASE, IANR RESEARCH ADDRESSES HEALTH AND DISEASE PROBLEMS THAT EXIST PRESLAUGHTER OR PRE‐COLLECTION OF ANIMAL PRODUCTS (PRE‐HARVEST). positiveFlows.title: UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS SYSTEM DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE (DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE) FACULTY, STAFF AND FACILITIES ARE LOCATED ON SEVEN UNIVERSITY CAMPUSES, FOUR RESEARCH AND EXTENSION CENTERS, SIX RESEARCH STATIONS, TWO EXTENSION CENTERS, AND IN ALL 75 COUNTIES. A FIFTH REGIONAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION CENTER IS CURRENTLY UNDER CONSTRUCTION. THE DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE REMAINS COMMITTED TO THIS STATEWIDE INFRASTRUCTURE WITH A PRESENCE IN ALL 75 ARKANSAS COUNTIES, ENSURING THAT RESEARCHERS AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS ARE READILY AVAILABLE TO ADDRESS THE SCIENCE AND BUSINESS OF AGRICULTURE AND THE BROADER NEEDS OF FAMILIES AND THE COMMUNITIES WE SERVE. CONSISTENT WITH THE LAND GRANT MISSION, DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION FACULTY HAVE A LONG HISTORY OF PROVIDING LEADERSHIP IN THE DEVELOPMENT, DISSEMINATION AND DELIVERY OF INNOVATIVE PRACTICES AND EMERGING TECHNOLOGY. DIVISION RESEARCHERS CONDUCT BASIC AND APPLIED RESEARCH FOR ARKANSAS PRODUCERS, BUSINESSES, COMMUNITIES, AND FAMILIES. COUNTY AGENTS AND SPECIALISTS STRIVE TO PROVIDE THE BEST SCIENCE‐BASED RECOMMENDATIONS AVAILABLE. ALTHOUGH STAKEHOLDERS ARE EXPOSED TO MULTIPLE SOURCES AND COPIOUS AMOUNTS OF INFORMATION AND DATA, THE DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE REMAINS A RELIABLE SOURCE OF IMPARTIAL AND SCIENCE‐BASED RECOMMENDATIONS, INDEPENDENT OF FINANCIAL OR PHILOSOPHICAL INTERESTS. ALTHOUGH MOST IN‐PERSON EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITIES HAVE RESUMED, THE DIVISION WILL CONTINUE TO DELIVER TIMELY AND RESPONSIVE DISTANCE EDUCATION WEBINARS AND RESOURCES IN 2023 TO ENSURE WIDE‐SPREAD ACCESS TO EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS BY ARKANSANS. THIS INCLUDES MONTHLY WEBINARS THROUGH THE NATIONAL AGRICULTURAL LAW CENTER ON CURRENT AND EMERGING IMPORTANT AGRICULTURAL, ENVIRONMENTAL AND FOOD LAW TOPICS. ONLINE COURSES ARE AVAILABLE 24/7/365 THROUGH THE DIVISION’S WEBSITE (HTTP://COURSES.UADA.EDU). DIVISION FACULTY ALSO ADDRESS TIMELY TOPICS OF INTEREST TO ARKANSANS THROUGH VIRTUAL EVENTS AND OTHER WEB‐BASED PROGRAMMING. THE FOCUS OF WORK CONDUCTED BY THE DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE CONTINUES TO BE GUIDED ANNUALLY BY GRASSROOTS, COMMUNITY‐BASED INPUT FROM A DIVERSE RANGE OF ARKANSAS CITIZENS; MAINLY THROUGH THE USE OF COUNTY EXTENSION COUNCILS AND OTHER LOCAL AND PROGRAM ADVISORY GROUPS. THE DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE FORMALLY ENGAGED A LARGE POOL OF STAKEHOLDERS (INCLUDING INDIVIDUAL CLIENTELE, PRODUCERS, SCHOOLS, PARTNER AGENCIES AND ORGANIZATIONS, STATE GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, COMMUNITY LEADERS, UNDERSERVED GROUPS, AND LEGISLATORS) IN THE DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE 2017‐2023 STRATEGIC PLAN. BASED ON BROAD STAKEHOLDER FEEDBACK, THE DIVISION IDENTIFIED FIVE AREAS TO FOCUS OUR EFFORTS: AGRICULTURAL AND FORESTRY PRODUCTION AND PROCESSING, ACCESS TO SAFE AND NUTRITIOUS FOOD, STRENGTHENING ARKANSAS FAMILIES, BUILDING COMMUNITIES AND STRENGTHENING ECONOMIES, AND NATURAL RESOURCE CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT. THESE FIVE EMPHASIS AREAS HELP TO PROVIDE STRATEGIC LOCAL GUIDANCE FOR DIVISION RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS AND HELP TO SUPPORT INTEGRATED RESEARCH/EXTENSION EFFORTS THAT ALIGN WITH THE NIFA SCIENCE EMPHASIS AREAS.  AGRICULTURAL AND FORESTRY PRODUCTION AND PROCESSING A CRITICAL NEED IN ARKANSAS, AND NATIONWIDE, IS TO ENSURE FARM AND FOREST ENTERPRISES ARE PROFITABLE AND SUSTAINABLE TO MEET THE DEMANDS FOR SAFE FOOD, FIBER, AND FUEL. THE AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY MUST CONTEND WITH MORE REGULATIONS, HIGHER INPUT COSTS, FLUCTUATING COMMODITY PRICES, CLIMATE EXTREMES, AND GLOBAL TRADE POLICIES. THE DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS WILL FOCUS ON INCREASING PRODUCTIVITY IN A HUMANE AND SUSTAINABLE MANNER WHILE DECREASING COSTS THROUGH EFFICIENT USE OF RESOURCES. PLANT SYSTEMS EMPHASIZE ECONOMICS, ENVIRONMENT, GENETICS AND BREEDING, WEEDS, DISEASE, PEST MANAGEMENT, SAFE HANDLING AND STORAGE, FOOD PROCESSING, CULTURAL PRACTICES, AND SOIL FERTILITY.  ANIMAL SYSTEMS EMPHASIZE GENETICS, REPRODUCTION, ECONOMICS, NUTRITION, WASTE MANAGEMENT, PHYSIOLOGY, ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS, HEALTH, AND ANIMAL WELLBEING. COMMON TO BOTH PLANT AND ANIMAL SYSTEMS IS THE APPROPRIATE USE OF NEW PRODUCTS AND TECHNOLOGY.  ACCESS TO SAFE AND NUTRITIOUS FOODS THE AVAILABILITY OF SAFE AND NUTRITIOUS FOOD IS VITAL TO FAMILIES AND INDIVIDUALS IN ALL COMMUNITIES. THE DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE WORKS TO PROMOTE HEALTHY DIETS THROUGH RESEARCH AND PUBLIC EDUCATION EFFORTS THAT TARGET OBESITY AND ENCOURAGE BETTER CONSUMER HABITS THROUGH PROGRAMS SUCH AS THE EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (EFNEP) AND SNAP‐ED. EFNEP EMPOWERS INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES WITH CHILDREN, WITH LIMITED INCOME, TO ACQUIRE KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ATTITUDE, AND BEHAVIOR CHANGES NECESSARY TO MAINTAIN NUTRITIONALLY SOUND DIETS AND ENHANCE PERSONAL DEVELOPMENT. SNAP‐ED PROVIDES NUTRITION EDUCATION TO FOOD STAMP RECIPIENTS AND THOSE INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES WHO ARE ELIGIBLE TO RECEIVE NUTRITION ASSISTANCE TO HELP CONSUMERS MAKE BETTER CHOICES ABOUT WHAT TO EAT TO STAY ACTIVE AND LIVE BETTER. THE DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE SEEKS TO STRENGTHEN FOOD SYSTEMS THROUGH RESEARCH AND INNOVATION. THE LONGTERM GROWTH OF THE FOOD INDUSTRY IN ARKANSAS IS DEPENDENT UPON THE INDUSTRY’S ABILITY TO INNOVATE, TO RESPOND TO CONSUMERS’ TASTE AND EXPECTATIONS, TO EMPLOY A QUALITY WORKFORCE AND TO MINIMIZE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS AND THE USE OF NATURAL RESOURCES WHILE MAINTAINING ECONOMIC VIABILITY. PARTNERSHIPS WITH COMMUNITY LEADERS AND AGENCIES ARE PURSUED TO INCREASE ACCESS TO NUTRITIOUS FOODS. EXTENSION PROGRAMS HELP PEOPLE FROM MANY BACKGROUNDS UNDERSTAND HOW TO MAKE WISE NUTRITIONAL CHOICES AND STRETCH FOOD DOLLARS BY COOKING FOR THEMSELVES AND UTILIZE A WIDER VARIETY OF FOODS. THE DIVISION ALSO STRIVES TO ENHANCE FOOD SAFETY THROUGH RESEARCH AND TEACHING BEST PRACTICES TO ALL WHO HANDLE FOOD, FROM FIELD TO TABLE. THIS INCLUDES EDUCATION RELATED TO FEDERAL AND STATE LAWS, SUCH AS HOW TO ADHERE TO THE FDA’S PRODUCE SAFETY RULE AND MEETING CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS OF THE ARKANSAS DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH THROUGH SERVSAFE, A FOOD SAFETY CERTIFICATION PROGRAM FOR INDIVIDUALS WHO WORK IN FOOD HANDLING OR FOOD SERVICE AND RELATED INDUSTRIES. EXTENSION EDUCATORS PROVIDE EVIDENCE‐BASED INFORMATION TO ENSURE THAT ARKANSANS ARE EQUIPPED WITH THE BEST FOOD SAFETY INFORMATION TO KEEP THEIR FAMILIES SAFE FROM FOODBORNE ILLNESSES AND OTHER FOOD‐RELATED SAFETY ISSUES. STRENGTHENING ARKANSAS FAMILIES  IT IS CRITICAL TO ADDRESS CHALLENGES THAT AFFECT FAMILIES, CONSUMERS, AND THE COMMUNITIES IN WHICH THEY LIVE. THE MENTAL, PHYSICAL, AND FINANCIAL WELL‐BEING OF FAMILIES AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF YOUTH ARE ESSENTIAL TO BUILDING PROSPERITY FOR ARKANSANS. THE DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE IS RESPONDING TO THESE NEEDS BY DELIVERING RESEARCH‐BASED PROGRAMS TO REDUCE STRESS, IMPROVE MENTAL HEALTH, STRENGTHEN RELATIONSHIPS, INCREASE FINANCIAL STABILITY, AND IMPROVE WELL‐BEING FOR ARKANSANS. 4‐H CLUBS, ACTIVITIES AND EVENTS ACROSS ARKANSAS INVOLVE YOUNG PEOPLE IN HANDS‐ON EDUCATION AND SERVICE‐LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES THAT ENHANCED THEIR LIFE SKILLS, INCLUDING DECISION MAKING, PROBLEM SOLVING, CRITICAL THINKING, COMMUNICATIONS, AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLE CHOICES. 4‐H CONVEYS TO THE PUBLIC THAT ALL YOUTH HAVE VALUE. STRIVING TO REACH A DIVERSE POPULATION IS KEY TO DEVELOPING CURRICULUM, OFFERING RECOGNITION, AND TEACHING STRONG LEADERSHIP SKILLS TO REPRESENT OUR STATE’S CURRENT DEMOGRAPHICS. BUILDING COMMUNITIES AND STRENGTHENING ECONOMIES  CHANGES IN THE ECONOMY, TECHNOLOGY AND POPULATION ARE TRANSFORMING HOW ARKANSANS LIVE AND WORK. THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED FOR BUSINESSES TO UNDERSTAND THEIR CHANGING ECONOMIC ENVIRONMENT AND EFFECTIVELY EMPLOY TOOLS AND RESOURCES. AT THE SAME TIME, THE LABOR FORCE REQUIRES ENHANCED SKILLS AND TRAINING TO SUCCEED IN TODAY’S GLOBAL ECONOMY. AT A TIME WHEN MANY RURAL AREAS ARE LOSING POPULATION, COMMUNITIES MUST TAKE A PROACTIVE APPROACH TO CREATE A HIGH QUALITY OF LIFE AND PLACE IF THEY WANT TO SURVIVE. EFFECTIVE AND INCLUSIVE LEADERS WORKING WITH ENGAGED CITIZENS ARE KEY TO THIS EFFORT. TO ADDRESS THESE CRITICAL NEEDS, PROGRAMS FOCUS ON FOUR AREAS: ECONOMIC VIABILITY AND SUSTAINABILITY; ENTREPRENEURSHIP IN EVOLVING ECONOMIES; LEADERSHIP AND CIVIC ENGAGEMENT; AND QUALITY OF LIFE AND PLACE.  NATURAL RESOURCE CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT ARKANSAS FACES CRITICAL NATURAL RESOURCE ISSUES INCLUDING GROUNDWATER DECLINE IN EASTERN ARKANSAS FROM IRRIGATION, WATER QUALITY CONCERNS FROM ANIMAL MANURES, SEDIMENT LOSS FROM CROPLAND AND URBAN STORMWATER. WE ALL SHARE CONCERNS FOR SOIL HEALTH, AIR QUALITY, PROTECTION OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES OF FORESTS AND WILDLIFE HABITAT, BUT AGRICULTURE IS UNDER SCRUTINY TO REDUCE IMPACT ON NATURAL RESOURCES. WE FOCUS ON UNBIASED RESEARCH AND SCIENCE‐BASED EXTENSION EFFORTS TO BALANCE CONSERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES. PROGRAMS, SUCH AS ARKANSAS DISCOVERY FARMS AND THE CENTER FOR AGRICULTURAL AND RURAL SUSTAINABILITY, WILL COLLABORATE WITH FARMERS, LANDOWNERS, AND INDUSTRY TO DELIVER INNOVATIVE, SUSTAINABLE PROGRAMS TO ENSURE PROPER CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES. IN ADDITION TO ANNUAL STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES TO INFORM RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS, THE DIVISION WILL LAUNCH A FORMAL AND COMPREHENSIVE EFFORT IN 2023 TO IDENTIFY PRIORITIES FOR THE ORGANIZATION’S NEW STRATEGIC PLAN WITH INPUT FROM STAKEHOLDERS THAT REPRESENT THE DIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS.

PI: ALONSO GUEDES GUEDE003@UMN.EDU, CO IS: TROY TRUMBLE, CATHY CARLSON BACKGROUND/PROBLEM:  OSTEOARTHRITIS (OA) IS HIGHLY PREVALENT IN ANIMALS AND HUMANS;  THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR THERAPIES THAT CAN EFFECTIVELY MITIGATE OA ASSOCIATED PAIN, DISABILITY AND JOINT PATHOLOGY;  A THERAPY WITH THESE QUALITIES WOULD HAVE A HIGH SOCIOECONOMIC IMPACT IN BOTH ANIMAL AND HUMAN HEALTH/MEDICINE. OBJECTIVE: TO ELUCIDATE THE INTERACTION BETWEEN TWO COX ISOFORMS (COX 1 AND COX 2) AND SEH IN APOPTOSIS OF EQUINE PRIMARY ARTICULAR CHONDROCYTES AND (II) THEIR EFFECTS ON REACTIVITY OF PRIMARY SENSORY NEURONS. BENEFITS OF PROPOSED RESEARCH/ EXPECTED OUTCOMES AND IMPACT:  WE BELIEVE, BASED ON STRONG PRELIMINARY DATA, THAT IT IS IMPORTANT TO UNDERSTAND THE INTERACTION BETWEEN SEH THE COX ISOFORMS IN MEDIATING CHONDROCYTE APOPTOSIS AND HYPERREACTIVITY OF SENSORY NEURONS IN ORDER TO GUIDE DEVELOPMENT OF A NOVEL ANALGESIC THERAPY FOR OA. SUCH DEVELOPMENT WILL VERTICALLY ADVANCE THE MOST COMMON OA THERAPY, WHICH IS BASED ON COX INHIBITION ALONE BUT IS OFTEN INADEQUATE FOR PAIN RELIEF, HAVE NO DISEASE MODIFYING EFFECT AND CAN CAUSE SIGNIFICANT ADVERSE EFFECTS. OUR RESULTS WILL SUPPORT FUTURE GRANT APPLICATIONS TO DEVELOP THIS TECHNOLOGY FOR THE CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF NATURALLY OCCURRING OA IN HORSES AND POSSIBLY OTHER SPECIES. WHAT ARE THE RISKS?  THERE IS SOME RISK THAT DATA OBTAINED IN CELL CULTURES MAY NOT ENTIRELY RECAPITULATE THE NATURALLY OCCURRING DISEASE. ADDITIONALLY, SOME PATHOGENS THAT CAUSE DISEASE IN POULTRY CAN ALSO CAUSE HUMAN HEALTH RISKS FROM CONSUMPTION OF IMPROPERLY PREPARED, CONTAMINATED EGGS AND MEAT. THE FIRST PROJECT FOCUSES ON METRITIS, A UTERINE DISEASE OF CRITICAL RELEVANCE TO THE DAIRY INDUSTRY WORLDWIDE. METRITIS IS ONE MAJOR REASON FOR ANTIMICROBIAL USE IN LIVESTOCK, AND IS ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED PRODUCTION COSTS, DECREASED YIELDS OF MILK, AND INCREASED MORTALITY AND CULLING OF LACTATING COWS. INFERTILITY IS AMONG THE MAIN DETRIMENTS CAUSED BY METRITIS AND REDUCING PREGNANCY IN SICK ANIMALS. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO DETERMINE KEY CHANGES IN UTERINE BIOLOGY ASSOCIATED WITH INFERTILITY SUBSEQUENT TO UTERINE DISEASES, SO THAT BETTER PREVENTIVE AND THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES CAN BE DEVISED TO IMPROVE ANIMAL HEALTH AND SUSTAINABILITY OF THE DAIRY INDUSTRY. THE DESCRIBED STUDIES WILL DEFINE CHANGES IN UTERINE MICROBIOME THAT ARE ASSOCIATED WITH LOSS OF FERTILITY IN COWS DIAGNOSED WITH METRITIS POSTPARTUM. THE SECOND PROJECT FOCUSES ON THE LACK OF KNOWLEDGE REGARDING THE EFFECTS OF HEAT STRESS ABATEMENT STRATEGIES, AND BIOLOGICAL FUNCTIONS OF YOUNG STOCK. THE THERMOREGULATION ABILITY OF CALVES IS MINIMAL DURING THE FIRST TEN DAYS OF LIFE AND INCREASES UNTIL 60 DAYS EXACERBATING THE NEED FOR STRATEGIES TO CONTROL THE ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH THEY ARE RAISED. THE DESCRIBED STUDIES WILL DETERMINE HOW HEAT ABATEMENT STRATEGIES IMPACTS ON THE WELL-BEING OF ANIMALS AND THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE STAKEHOLDERS IT SERVES. SUCH STUDIES ARE OF IMPORTANCE TO INVESTIGATE AND MITIGATE THE EFFECTS OF HEAT STRESS AND CLIMATE CHANGE ON ANIMAL WELL-BEING AND HEALTH. THE THIRD PROJECT FOCUSES ON SPOTTY LIVER DISEASE (SLD) CAUSED BY CAMPYLOBACTER HEPATICUS. SLD IS AN EMERGING CAUSE OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY AND LOSS OF PRODUCTION IN COMMERCIAL LAYING HENS. CURRENTLY, THE DISEASE IS CONTROLLED BY TREATING THE AFFECTED FLOCKS WITH ANTIBIOTICS, BUT THE EMERGENCE OF ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE IS NEGATIVELY IMPACTING THE ANTIBIOTIC-FREE LAYER INDUSTRY. THE DESCRIBED STUDY WILL TEST VACCINATION WITH VARIOUS C. HEPATICUS PROTEINS TO DETERMINE EXTENT OF PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY CONFERRED TO CONTROL SLD. SUCH APPROACH SHOULD ALLOW FOR ADEQUATE IMMUNITY BE INDUCED DURING PEAK EGG PRODUCTION, AT WHICH TIME, BIRDS ARE MOST SUSCEPTIBLE TO SLD. RESULTS FROM THESE STUDIES WILL IMPROVE ANIMAL HEALTH MANAGEMENT AND REDUCE THE RELIANCE ON ANTIMICROBIALS BY LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS.

positiveFlows.title: THE FUNDS WILL BE USED TO MAINTAIN AND ENHANCE THE INFRASTRUCTURE THAT SUPPORTS RESEARCH AIMED AT IMPROVING THE HEALTH AND WELLBEING OF PRODUCTION ANIMALS AND EQUIDS. THE FUNDS WILL SUPPORT TWO SPECIFIC RESEARCH PROJECTS. THE GOAL OF THE FIRST PROJECT IS TO IMPROVE THE MANAGEMENT OF SEPSIS, A COMMON AND OFTEN FATAL CONDITION IN HORSES AND CAMELIDS AND OCCASIONALLY OTHER DOMESTIC ANIMALS. SEPSIS IS AN INFECTION THAT CAUSES SYSTEMIC (WHOLE BODY) INFLAMMATION. THIS OFTEN COMPROMISES THE BLOOD CIRCULATION AND FUNCTION OF VITAL ORGANS LEADING TO DEATH. A COMMON COMPLICATION IN HORSES IS LAMINITIS, A VERY PAINFUL CONDITION IN WHICH THE HOOF SEPARATES FROM THE UNDERLYING BONE. EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS FOR SEPSIS AND LAMINITIS ARE LACKING. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A ROBUST AND PREDICTABLE ANIMAL MODEL OF SEPSIS WHICH WILL ALLOW THE EVALUATION OF POTENTIAL NEW THERAPIES. A SECOND LINE OF RESEARCH AIMS TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFECT OF A DRUG THAT PREVENTS PLATELET AGGREGATION AND THEREFORE IMPROVES THE BLOOD CIRCULATION ON LAMINITIS. THE RESEARCH IS EXPECTED TO LEAD TO THE DISCOVERY OF NEW TREATMENTS FOR SEPSIS IN HORSES AND OTHER SPECIES. THIS WILL BE OF GREAT INTEREST TO HORSE BREEDERS, HORSE OWNERS, OWNERS OF CAMELIDS AND VETERINARY PRACTITIONERS. THE RESULTS OF THESE STUDIES WILL BE DISSEMINATED THROUGH SCIENTIFIC AND LAY PUBLICATIONS AS WELL AS PRESENTATIONS AT REGIONAL AND NATIONAL MEETINGS. THE WORK WILL BE PERFORMED WITH VETERINARY STUDENTS, RESIDENTS AND GRADUATE STUDENTS WHO WILL RECEIVE IMPORTANT HANDS-ON RESEARCH TRAINING AND GAIN PRACTICAL CLINICAL EXPERIENCE. THE SECOND PROJECT FOCUSES ON EQUINE PROTOZOAL MYELOENCEPHALITIS (EPM), A NEUROLOGIC DISEASE CAUSED BY SARCOCYSTIS NEURONA THAT RESULTS IN HUGE ECONOMIC LOSSES TO THE EQUINE INDUSTRY. S. NEURONA INFECTS BETWEEN 15 AND 89% OF HORSES, BUT CLINICAL DISEASE DEVELOPS IN LESS THAN 1% OF THESE HORSES. THE PROGRESSION OF THIS NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE IS UNPREDICTABLE AND OFTEN TIMES REQUIRES PROLONGED TREATMENT WITH ANTIPROTOZOAL DRUGS THAT ARE EXPENSIVE. UNFORTUNATELY, ONLY 60-70% OF THE HORSES APPEAR TO RESPOND TO TREATMENT AND 10-20% OF THE HORSES EXPERIENCE RELAPSE OF CLINICAL SIGNS UPON CESSATION OF TREATMENT. SARCOCYSTIS NEURONA ESTABLISHES INFECTION WITHIN THE CELLS OF THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. UNDERSTANDING HOW S. NEURONA SURVIVES WITHIN, AND INTERACTS WITH THE HOST CELL WILL PROVIDE INSIGHTS INTO MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT COULD BE TARGETED TO PREVENT RELAPSE FROM OCCURRING. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO IDENTIFY KEY PARASITE PROTEINS THAT SUPPORT ITS INTRACELLULAR LIFESTYLE, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF MOLECULAR GENETICS TOOLS THAT WILL ENABLE US TO DECIPHER THE BIOLOGICAL ROLE OF THESE PROTEINS. THESE EFFORTS WILL LEAD TO IDENTIFICATION OF PROTEINS (SECRETORY AND MEMBRANE) THAT ARE FUNCTIONAL DURING INTRACELLULAR DEVELOPMENT OF S. NEURONA, AND POTENTIAL TARGETS FOR DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL DRUGS TO TREAT THESE INFECTIONS. THE IMMEDIATE TARGET AUDIENCE FOR THIS WORK WILL BE OTHER SCIENTISTS IN ACADEMIC AND ANIMAL HEALTH COMPANIES. THE OUTCOME IS THE IDENTIFICATION OF PROTEINS THAT ARE CRITICAL FOR THE INTRACELLULAR SURVIVAL AND FUNCTION OF THE PARASITES. THE RESULTS OF THE RESEARCH WILL BE DISSEMINATED THROUGH PUBLICATIONS AND PRESENTATIONS AT NATIONAL MEETINGS

POULTRY: THE US POULTRY INDUSTRY IS A MULTIBILLION-DOLLAR INDUSTRY THAT ANNUALLY LOSES UP TO 15% OF ITS POTENTIAL INCOME DUE TO DISEASE. THESE ECONOMIC LOSSES ARE FROM MANY SOURCES, INCLUDING ANIMAL MORTALITY, HEALTH CARE COSTS, PRODUCT CONDEMNATION, AND LOWER EFFICIENCY OF PRODUCTION. ADDITIONALLY, SOME PATHOGENS THAT CAUSE DISEASE IN POULTRY CAN ALSO CAUSE HUMAN HEALTH RISKS FROM CONSUMPTION OF IMPROPERLY PREPARED, CONTAMINATED EGGS AND MEAT. THE FUNDS WILL SUPPORT TWO SPECIFIC RESEARCH PROJECTS. THE GOAL OF THE FIRST PROJECT IS TO IMPROVE THE MANAGEMENT OF SEPSIS, A COMMON AND OFTEN FATAL CONDITION IN HORSES AND CAMELIDS AND OCCASIONALLY OTHER DOMESTIC ANIMALS. SEPSIS IS AN INFECTION THAT CAUSES SYSTEMIC (WHOLE BODY) INFLAMMATION. THIS OFTEN COMPROMISES THE BLOOD CIRCULATION AND FUNCTION OF VITAL ORGANS LEADING TO DEATH. A COMMON COMPLICATION IN HORSES IS LAMINITIS, A VERY PAINFUL CONDITION IN WHICH THE HOOF SEPARATES FROM THE UNDERLYING BONE. EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS FOR SEPSIS AND LAMINITIS ARE LACKING. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A ROBUST AND PREDICTABLE ANIMAL MODEL OF SEPSIS WHICH WILL ALLOW THE EVALUATION OF POTENTIAL NEW THERAPIES. A SECOND LINE OF RESEARCH AIMS TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFECT OF A DRUG THAT PREVENTS PLATELET AGGREGATION AND THEREFORE IMPROVES THE BLOOD CIRCULATION ON LAMINITIS. THE RESEARCH IS EXPECTED TO LEAD TO THE DISCOVERY OF NEW TREATMENTS FOR SEPSIS IN HORSES AND OTHER SPECIES. THIS WILL BE OF GREAT INTEREST TO HORSE BREEDERS, HORSE OWNERS, OWNERS OF CAMELIDS AND VETERINARY PRACTITIONERS. THE RESULTS OF THESE STUDIES WILL BE DISSEMINATED THROUGH SCIENTIFIC AND LAY PUBLICATIONS AS WELL AS PRESENTATIONS AT REGIONAL AND NATIONAL MEETINGS. THE WORK WILL BE PERFORMED WITH VETERINARY STUDENTS, RESIDENTS AND GRADUATE STUDENTS WHO WILL RECEIVE IMPORTANT HANDS-ON RESEARCH TRAINING AND GAIN PRACTICAL CLINICAL EXPERIENCE. THE SECOND PROJECT FOCUSES ON EQUINE PROTOZOAL MYELOENCEPHALITIS (EPM), A NEUROLOGIC DISEASE CAUSED BY SARCOCYSTIS NEURONA THAT RESULTS IN HUGE ECONOMIC LOSSES TO THE EQUINE INDUSTRY. S. NEURONA INFECTS BETWEEN 15 AND 89% OF HORSES, BUT CLINICAL DISEASE DEVELOPS IN LESS THAN 1% OF THESE HORSES. THE PROGRESSION OF THIS NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE IS UNPREDICTABLE AND OFTEN TIMES REQUIRES PROLONGED TREATMENT WITH ANTIPROTOZOAL DRUGS THAT ARE EXPENSIVE. UNFORTUNATELY, ONLY 60-70% OF THE HORSES APPEAR TO RESPOND TO TREATMENT AND 10-20% OF THE HORSES EXPERIENCE RELAPSE OF CLINICAL SIGNS UPON CESSATION OF TREATMENT. SARCOCYSTIS NEURONA ESTABLISHES INFECTION WITHIN THE CELLS OF THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. UNDERSTANDING HOW S. NEURONA SURVIVES WITHIN, AND INTERACTS WITH THE HOST CELL WILL PROVIDE INSIGHTS INTO MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT COULD BE TARGETED TO PREVENT RELAPSE FROM OCCURRING. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO IDENTIFY KEY PARASITE PROTEINS THAT SUPPORT ITS INTRACELLULAR LIFESTYLE, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF MOLECULAR GENETICS TOOLS THAT WILL ENABLE US TO DECIPHER THE BIOLOGICAL ROLE OF THESE PROTEINS. THESE EFFORTS WILL LEAD TO IDENTIFICATION OF PROTEINS (SECRETORY AND MEMBRANE) THAT ARE FUNCTIONAL DURING INTRACELLULAR DEVELOPMENT OF S. NEURONA, AND POTENTIAL TARGETS FOR DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL DRUGS TO TREAT THESE INFECTIONS. THE IMMEDIATE TARGET AUDIENCE FOR THIS WORK WILL BE OTHER SCIENTISTS IN ACADEMIC AND ANIMAL HEALTH COMPANIES. THE OUTCOME IS THE IDENTIFICATION OF PROTEINS THAT ARE CRITICAL FOR THE INTRACELLULAR SURVIVAL AND FUNCTION OF THE PARASITES. THE RESULTS OF THE RESEARCH WILL BE DISSEMINATED THROUGH PUBLICATIONS AND PRESENTATIONS AT NATIONAL MEETINGS.

PROJECT TITLE: DEVELOPMENT OF HEALTHY AQUACULTURE ENVIRONMENT THROUGH CONTROL OF DISEASE-CAUSING PATHOGENS AND STRENGTHENING FISH HEALTH EDUCATION IN ALABAMA STATE  ABSTRACT: GLOBALLY, AQUACULTURE PRODUCTION HAS INCREASED FROM 34.6 MILLION TONS IN 2007 TO 55.7 MILLION TONS IN 2009. AQUACULTURE PRODUCTION IN THE UNITED STATES FOR FIN FISH EXCEEDS 500,000 TONS AND SALES ESTIMATED AT $1.37 BILLION IN 2003. CATFISH INDUSTRY ACCOUNTS FOR 40% OF THIS PRODUCTION GROWN MAINLY IN MISSISSIPPI, ALABAMA, ARKANSAS, AND LOUISIANA. ALABAMA IS THE SECOND AQUACULTURE PRODUCER NATIONWIDE. IN 2016 ALABAMA CATFISH PRODUCTION WAS 34% OF THE ENTIRE CATFISH PRODUCTION NATIONWIDE AND PROVIDED JOBS FOR MORE THAN 26 HUNDRED INDIVIDUALS AND THE MAIN AQUACULTURE CATFISH PRODUCTION IS HARVESTED FROM BLACK-BELT COUNTIES. BACTERIAL INFECTIONS ARE THE MAIN RISK FOR THE INDUSTRY. IN COMMERCIAL FARMING, FISH GET MORE INFECTIOUS DISEASES UNLIKE FISH IN THE NATURAL HABITAT. THIS IS DUE TO MANY FACTORS BUT MAINLY THE HUSBANDRY- RELATED FACTORS PLAY THE LEADING CAUSES OF DISEASE. INFECTIOUS DISEASES POSE ONE OF THE MOST SIGNIFICANT THREATS TO SUCCESSFUL AQUACULTURE. THE MAINTENANCE OF LARGE NUMBERS OF FISH CROWDED TOGETHER IN A SMALL AREA PROVIDES AN ENVIRONMENT CONDUCIVE FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND SPREAD OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES. IN THIS CROWDED, RELATIVELY UNNATURAL ENVIRONMENT, FISH ARE STRESSED AND MORE SUSCEPTIBLE TO DISEASE. MOREOVER, THE WATER ENVIRONMENT, AND LIMITED WATER FLOW, FACILITATES THE SPREAD OF PATHOGENS WITHIN THE CROWDED POPULATIONS. AMONG THESE PATHOGENS, BACTERIA ARE MORE IMPORTANT BECAUSE OF EASY SPREAD AND THE DAMAGE THEY CAUSE TO THE FISH AND AQUACULTURE INDUSTRY IS SUBSTANTIAL. EDWARDSIELLA SPP., AEROMONAS SPP., FLAVOBACTERIUM COLUMNARIS AND STREPTOCOCCUS INIAE ARE THE MOST IMPORTANT BACTERIA THAT POSE GREAT HEALTH THREAT TO FRESHWATER FISH INDUSTRY IN ALABAMA. SOME ARE ZOONOTIC PATHOGEN E.G. EDWARSIELLA TARDA ,<(>,<)> STREPTOCOCCUS INIAE, THEY ARE ALSO OF GREAT PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERN. THIS PROJECT AIMS AT CONTROLLING BACTERIAL DISEASES THROUGH IMPROVING QUALITY OF WATER AND EDUCATE AQUACULTURE FARMERS, EXTENSION OFFICIALS OF THE HEALTH HAZARDS TO FISH INDUSTRY AND HOW TO MITIGATE IT. HERE WE WILL TARGET THE FISH HABITAT BY STUDYING THE PATHOGENS COEXIST WITH THE FISH. THEIR NUMBERS AND DISTRIBUTION MUST BE UNDER CONTINUOUS CONTROL. THE PROJECT WILL STUDY FISH PATHOGENS IN TERMS OF VIRULENCE CHARACTERS AND ANTIBIOTIC SENSITIVITY PATTERN. THIS STUDY WILL BE OF GREAT INTEREST TO HEALTH, EXTENSION OFFICIALS AND FISH FARMERS. THE PROJECT WILL SPREAD AQUACULTURE HEALTH KNOWLEDGE THROUGH EDUCATION TO GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS AND FISH  TECHNICIANS. METHODS: WATER AND FRESH CATFISH SAMPLES WILL BE COLLECTED FROM STUDY AREA (BLACK BELT COUNTIES). CONVENTIONAL MICROBIOLOGICAL PROCEDURES WILL APPLY TO DETECT PATHOGENS OF INTEREST (AEROMONAS, EDWARDSIELLA, AND FLAVOBACTERIUM). DETECTED ISOLATES WILL BE CHARACTERIZED FOR VIRULENCE FACTORS AND ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCEPATTERN. MOLECULAR STUDIES WILL ASSESS PRESENCE OF VIRULENCE AND ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE GENES. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY THE OREGON AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (OAES) AND THE OSU EXTENSION SERVICE (OSUES) AT OREGON STATE UNIVERSITY PROVIDE THE PEOPLE OF OREGON WITH RESEARCH-BASED KNOWLEDGE AND EDUCATION THAT FOCUS ON STRENGTHENING COMMUNITIES AND ECONOMIES, SUSTAINING NATURAL RESOURCES, AND PROMOTING HEALTHY FAMILIES AND INDIVIDUALS. OAES IS OREGON'S PRINCIPAL SOURCE OF KNOWLEDGE RELATING TO AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD SYSTEMS, AND A MAJOR SOURCE OF KNOWLEDGE REGARDING ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY, NATURAL RESOURCES, LIFE SCIENCES, AND RURAL ECONOMIES AND COMMUNITIES WORLDWIDE. OSUES WORKS TO USE RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION TO CREATE POSITIVE IMPACTS ON COMMUNITY LIVABILITY, ECONOMIC VITALITY, AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES SUSTAINABILITY, AND THE HEALTH AND WELL- BEING OF PEOPLE. PROJECTS AND PROGRAMS CONDUCTED BY OAES AND OSUES ARE COMPLEMENTARY AND CROSS DISCIPLINARY LINES TO MORE FULLY ADDRESS CRITICAL ISSUES AT THE LOCAL, REGIONAL AND NATIONAL LEVELS. THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES’ OAES OFFICE REFLECTS THESE VALUES: VALUE 1: RESPONSIVENESS - WE REACT IN A TIMELY FASHION TO THE NEEDS OF THOSE WE SERVE; VALUE 2: PARTNERSHIP AND COOPERATION - WE COLLABORATE WITH INDIVIDUALS, ORGANIZATIONS, BUSINESSES, AND AGENCIES OUTSIDE THE UNIVERSITY; VALUE 3: TEAMWORK AND COORDINATION - WE SYNCHRONIZE OUR EFFORTS AMONG OUR UNITS AND WITH OTHER UNITS AT THE UNIVERSITY; VALUE 4: CREDIBILITY - WE FOCUS ON BEING KNOWN AS A SOURCE OF RELIABLE, OBJECTIVE, RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION AND EDUCATION. THE CORE VALUES AND OPERATING PRINCIPLES OF OSUES ARE: VALUE 1: COMMUNITY-BASED - WE VALUE COMMUNITY RELATIONSHIPS AND CONNECT OSU TO LOCAL PEOPLE AND ISSUES TO ENHANCE THE PRESENT AND THE FUTURE OF THE PEOPLE AND COMMUNITIES OF OREGON. VALUE 2: ACCOUNTABILITY - WE FOCUS ON ACHIEVING MEASURABLE OUTCOMES, AND DOCUMENT AND COMMUNICATE THE IMPACT AND VALUE OF OUR WORK. VALUE 3: CREDIBILITY - WE DELIVER RELEVANT, RESEARCH-BASED KNOWLEDGE THROUGH OUR EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS. VALUE 4: DIVERSITY - WE EXHIBIT RESPECT, VALUE DIFFERING PERCEPTIONS AND WORLD VIEWS, AND ENCOURAGE DIVERSITY. VALUE 5: PARTNERSHIPS - WE COLLABORATE WITH ACADEMIC, PUBLIC, AND PRIVATE PARTNERS TO ACHIEVE GREATER RESULTS AND BUILD COMMUNITY CA PACITY. WE VALUE THE PUBLIC GOOD THAT COMES FROM COLLABORATING WITH VOLUNTEERS. VALUE 6: RESPONSIVENESS - WE ENGAGE WITH COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO IDENTIFY PRIORITY ISSUES AND NEEDS, TO DESIGN TIMELY RESPONSES, AND TO BUILD FUTURE CAPABILITY.  TO CARRY OUT ITS MISSION IN A MANNER CONSISTENT WITH UNIVERSITY GOALS, OAES USES ITS RESOURCES TO ADVANCE KNOWLEDGE IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS OF EMPHASIS: 1) NEW VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS AND MARKETS THAT LEVERAGE THE ECONOMIC CONTRIBUTIONS OF OREGON AGRICULTURE. 2) NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT AND POLICY THROUGH DISCOVERY AND LEARNING TO IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING OF OUR NATURAL AND WORKING LANDSCAPES AS A SYSTEM. 3) INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS THAT HELP ASSURE ECONOMICALLY SUSTAINABLE, ENVIRONMENTALLY SOUND AND RESILIENT AGRICULTURE.     THEOSUES GOALS FOR ADVANCING THE ORGANIZATION'S MISSION TO ALIGN WITH THE UNIVERSITY'S STRATEGIC PLANS INCLUDE: GOAL 1: IMPROVE ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY LEARNER SERVICES - EXTENSION PROVIDES ACCESS TO THE KNOWLEDGE RESOURCES OF OSU BY BEING FOCUSED AND NIMBLE IN ENGAGING OREGON'S DIVERSE PEOPLE AND COMMUNITIES IN HIGH-QUALITY LEANER SERVICES THAT HELP BUILD SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY FUTURES. GOAL 2: INVEST FOR EXCELLENCE AND IMPACT - EXTENSION WORKS TO INCREASE AND DIVERSITY ITS FUNDING BASE AND ENCOURAGE PROGRAM EXCELLENCE THROUGH STRATEGIC INVESTMENTS WITHIN FOUR THEMATIC AREAS: HEALTHY COMMUNITIES AND ECONOMIES; RESILIENT AND PRODUCTIVE FORESTRY AND NATURAL ECOSYSTEMS; SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, FOOD SYSTEMS, AND GARDENING; THRIVING YOUTH, INDIVIDUALS, AND FAMILIES. THIS WILL CREATE MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND IMPACTS THAT WILL BE REPORTED WIDELY TO STAKEHOLDERS. GOAL 3: INCREASE EFFECTIVENESS WITH APPROPRIATE TECHNOLOGY - EXTENSION USES ESTABLISHED AND NEW TECHNOLOGIES STRATEGICALLY TO INCREASE EFFICIENCIES, EXPAND OUTREACH AND ENHANCE AND REPORT THE OUTCOMES OF ITS EDUCATIONAL SERVICES.  THE AES STATION UNITS ACROSS THE STATE, UTILIZE INPUT FROM AFFILIATED ADVISORY COMMITTEES, FROM FACULTY RESEARCH EXPERTS, LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS INCLUDING FARMERS AND RANCHERS, FORESTERS, AGENCY PERSONNEL, ELECTED LEADERS, EDUCATORS, HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS, AND MYRIAD OTHER PUBLIC AND PRIVATE ENTITIES TO ESTABLISH NEED AND DESIGN APPROPRIATE PROGRAMMING. IN MANY CASES, STAKEHOLDERS ARE DIRECTLY INVOLVED IN THE PROGRAMMING AS VOLUNTEERS OR BY PERMITTING DEMONSTRATIONS AND APPLIED RESEARCH TRIALS ON THEIR PROPERTIES. WE RECENTLY AUGMENTED OUR ABILITIES TO CONNECT WITH STAKEHOLDERS ACROSS DIVERSE INTEREST AREAS AND TO GAIN ADVICE REGARDING FUTURE RESEARCH PRIORITIES FOR THE PEOPLE OF OREGON WITH THE FORMATION OF A RESEARCH COMMUNITY ADVISORY NETWORK (RCAN) TO PROVIDE INPUT TO THE OAES ON CURRENT AND FUTURE RESEARCH NEEDS. ADDITIONALLY, FACULTY MEMBERS UTILIZE CRITICAL DEMOGRAPHIC AND ECONOMIC DATA, AND EXAMINE CURRENT RESEARCH FINDINGS TO IDENTIFY SOCIETAL NEEDS AND OPPORTUNITIES FOR SIGNIFICANT SOCIAL, ENVIRONMENTAL, AND ECONOMIC IMPACTS. PROGRAMMING IS THEN PLANNED BASED ON INPUT WITHIN OAES, EXTERNAL ADVISORY GROUPS, AND IN EACH OTHER ACADEMIC COLLEGES/PROGRAMS (I.E. FORESTRY, AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES, HEALTH AND HUMAN SCIENCES) AND ASSOCIATED EXTENSION PROGRAMS.  INPUT IS SOLICITED BY OSUES THROUGH A STATEWIDE ADVISORY NETWORK KNOWN AS EXTENSION COMMUNITY ADVISORY NETWORK (ECAN) THAT DIRECTLY ADVISES THE VICE PROVOST FOR EXTENSION AND ENGAGEMENT AND DIRECTOR OF EXTENSION. THIS ADVISORY COMMITTEE IS MADE UP OF INDIVIDUALS REPRESENTING EACH OF OSUES’S SEVEN PROGRAM AREAS (4-H YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES, FAMILY AND COMMUNITY HEALTH, FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES, OPEN CAMPUS, OUTDOOR SCHOOL, AND SEA GRANT) AS WELL AS TWO COUNTY COMMISSIONERS AND ADDITIONAL REPRESENTATIVES FROM OREGON COUNTIES AS DETERMINED BY THE OSUES DIRECTOR. PLANNED OUTCOMES DEVELOPED FROM THIS PROCESS ARE OUTLINED IN A BIENNIAL PLAN SUBMITTED BY EACH PARTICIPATING COLLEGE.  OAES PROJECTS ARE REVIEWED ANNUALLY ON THE BASIS OF PLANNED OUTCOMES OUTLINED IN A FIVE-YEAR, PEER REVIEWED PROPOSAL SUBMITTED TO OAES AND APPROVED BY NIFA. PROJECT OUTCOMES ARE ALSO ASSESSED AGAINST THE AES’S INTERNAL STRATEGIC INTENT DOCUMENT, A STRATEGIC DIRECTIVE FORMULATED WITH INPUT FROM INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL STAKEHOLDERS. OAES HAS IDENTIFIED FOUR CRITICAL ISSUES THAT WILL BE ADDRESSED UNDER THE POW: 1) MARINE CONSERVATION AND FOOD SYSTEMS, 2) AGRICULTURAL COMPETITIVENESS AND RESILIENCE, 3) MARKETS AND ACCESS IN FOOD AND HEALTH INNOVATIONS, AND 4) WORKING AND NATURAL LANDSCAPES. THESE FOUR "THEMES" WILL DRIVE THE RESEARCH AND OUTREACH EFFORTS OF THE COLLEGE OVER THE REPORTING PERIOD. THE STRATEGIC CHALLENGES IDENTIFIED BY NIFA, WHICH TARGETED SUSTAINABLE ENERGY, CLIMATE CHANGE, GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY/HUNGER, FOOD SAFETY, AND OBESITY ARE EVIDENT ACROSS THE PLAN. AN ADDITIONAL CRITICAL ISSUE– ANIMAL HEALTH – HAS BEEN ADDED TO ADDRESS CAPACITY FUNDING ASSOCIATED WITH ANIMAL HEALTH AND DISEASE RESEARCH AS WELL AS OTHER COMPETITIVE GRANT FUNDING. THE CONNECTIVELY AND INTERACTIONS BETWEEN THE OAES AND OSUES AND THE OVERLAP IN THE STAKEHOLDER COMMUNITIES WE SERVE ULTIMATELY COMBINES TO RESULT IN ACCESS TO RESEARCH-BASED KNOWLEDGE AND EFFECTIVE PROGRAMMING THAT DELIVERS RESEARCH-BASED SOLUTIONS FOR CONTEMPORARY ISSUES TO ENABLE RESILIENCE IN AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND IMPROVED LIVELIHOODS FOR THE PEOPLE OF OREGON

TITLE OF PROJECT 1: MICRORNAS PRESENT IN BOVINE MILK AND THEIR ABILITY TO SHAPE THE NEONATAL IMMUNITY TO RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS ABSTRACT: NEWBORN CALVES LACK OF CIRCULATING ANTIBODIES. IN THE FIRST WEEKS OF LIFE, THE BOVINE NEONATE’S ABILITY TO FIGHT OFF PATHOGENS IS THEREFORE FULLY DEPENDENT UPON INGESTING COLOSTRUM (THE FIRST MILK PRODUCED BY FEMALE MAMMALS). THIS TRANSFER OF PASSIVE IMMUNITY IS CRUCIAL FOR THE NEWBORNS’ SURVIVAL DURING THE FIRST WEEKS OF LIFE, WHICH ARE THE MOST CHALLENGING PERIOD TO ENTERIC INFECTIONS. IN THIS SCENARIO, BOVINE RESPIRATORY DISEASE COMPLEX (A COMBINATION OF STRESS, VIRAL, AND BACTERIAL INFECTIONS) IS A MAJOR CAUSE OF MORTALITY IN NEONATAL CALVES. IN ADDITION TO ANTIBODIES AND NUTRITIONAL FACTORS (I.E., FAT, PROTEIN, MINERALS), COLOSTRUM CONTAINS A VARIETY OF BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS INCLUDING GROWTH FACTORS, CYTOKINES, MILK MICROBIOTA, AND RECENTLY MICRORNAS (MIRNAS) HAVE BEEN ADDED TO THE COLOSTRUM COMPOSITION LIST. MICRORNAS ARE SMALL NON‐CODING RNA MOLECULES, WHICH HAVE BEEN IMPLICATED IN REGULATING MRNA EXPRESSION AND PROTEIN TRANSCRIPTION. ADDITIONALLY, THEY HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO BE INVOLVED IN VARIOUS DISEASE STATES AND MAY HAVE A ROLE IN IMMUNE SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTION. FOR INSTANCE, MICRORNAS HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO REGULATE BAND T‐CELL DIFFERENTIATION AND AFFECT CYTOKINES PRODUCTION BY MACROPHAGES. IN HUMANS, MICRORNAS IN BREASTMILK VARY DUE TO ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, SUCH AS PRETERM BIRTH AND MATERNAL DIET, AND HAVE ALSO BEEN SHOWN TO ORIGINATE FROM THE MAMMARY GLAND AND NOT THE MOTHERS’ SYSTEMIC CIRCULATION. THUS, IT’S PLAUSIBLE TO EXPECT SIMILAR RESPONSES IN OTHER SPECIES WHERE MICRORNAS CAN SERVE AS SIGNALING MOLECULES PASSED FROM THE MOTHER TO THE NEWBORN TO ENHANCE THE RESPONSE TO NEONATAL INFECTIONS. THUS, THIS PROJECT AIMS TO IDENTIFY KEY MICRORNAS DERIVED FROM BOVINE COLOSTRUM THAT CAN REGULATE THE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE TO NEONATAL INFECTIONS. RATIONALE: BOVINE MICRORNAS HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO BE ABSORBED AND TRANSPORTED INTO SYSTEMIC CIRCULATION IN MICE. HOWEVER, THE ROLE OF SUCH MICRORNAS DERIVED FROM COLOSTRUM AND THEIR ROLE IN PROTECTING NEWBORN CALVES FROM RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS REMAIN TO BE DETERMINED. METHODOLOGY: FOR MICRORNA ISOLATION, ISOLATE MICRORNAS FROM BOVINE MILK (COLOSTRUM, TRANSITION MILK, AND MATURE MILK) AND THROUGH REAL TIME QPCR IDENTIFY THE MOST EXPRESSED MICRORNAS IN BOVINE MILK. IN VITRO STUDY: BOVINE PRIMARY LUNG CELLS (PURCHASED FROM ACCEGEN™) WILL BE CHALLENGED WITH ESCHERICHIA COLI LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDE (LPS) AND INCUBATED WITH A POOL OF MICRORNAS EXTRACTED FROM THE DIFFERENT MILK SAMPLES FOR 24 HOURS. ENDPOINT ASSAYS INCLUDING CYTOKINES MEASUREMENT AND FLOW CYTOMETRY ANALYSIS WILL BE PERFORMED TO EVALUATE THE IMMUNE RESPONSE TO THE INDUCED‐INFECTION IN THE CONTROL VS MICRORNA‐TREATED CELLS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES: FOR COMPOSITION OF MICRORNAS IN BOVINE MILK, WE WILL DETERMINE THE COMPOSITION OF MICRORNAS FROM COLOSTRUM VS. MATURE MILK. WITH THE MICRORNAS COMPOSITION FROM DIFFERENT STAGES OF LACTATION, WE CAN IDENTIFY THE COMMON MICRORNA PROFILE IN BOVINE MILK AND THE POTENTIAL MICRORNAS MARKERS THAT MIGHT IMPACT THE IMMUNE RESPONSE. IMPACT OF MICRORNAS ON IMMUNE SYSTEM: IMMUNE CELL REPERTOIRE, INCLUDING T CELLS, B CELLS, AND NEUTROPHILS WILL BE ENUMERATED USING FLOW CYTOMETRY ANALYSIS.

ANDREIA ARRUDA RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS CAUSED BY ORNITHOBACTERIUM RHINOTRACHEALIS (ORT) AND PASTEURELLA MULTOCIDA (PM) BACTERIA ARE SIGNIFICANT THREATS TO THE POULTRY INDUSTRY BY CAUSING ECONOMIC LOSSES AND WELFARE ISSUES. DUE TO CHARACTERIZATION DIFFICULTIES AND UNDERUTILIZATION OF EPIDEMIOLOGICAL TOOLS, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THE SPATIO-TEMPORAL SPREAD OF BACTERIAL SUBTYPES FOR THESE DISEASES IN THE FIELD. THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS RETROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY ARE TO A) DESCRIBE MOLECULAR CHARACTERIZATION AND SPACE-TIME PATTERNS FOR ORT AND PM USING ISOLATES COLLECTED FROM OUTBREAKS ON POULTRY FARMS; B) INVESTIGATE THE EXISTENCE OF SPATIAL CLUSTERS (HOTSPOTS) FOR ORT AND PM; AND C) INVESTIGATE THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN GENETIC SIMILARITY AND SPATIAL PROXIMITY FOR BOTH ORT AND PM. ANALYSIS WILL BE DONE SEPARATELY FOR EACH BACTERIA. negativeFlows.title: A TISSUE ENGINEERING APPROACH TO INVESTIGATE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN PATHOGENS AND MAMMALIAN CELLS, EUKARYOTIC CELL DEVELOPMENT, OR OTHER DISEASE STATES OF MAMMALIAN CELLS CAN BEST BE ACCOMPLISHED USING INNOVATIVE THREE-DIMENSIONAL (3-D) TISSUE CULTURES, OR ORGANOIDS. 3-D TISSUE CULTURES PRESENT A MORE PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT SYSTEM THAN SIMPLE 2-D TISSUE CULTURES. SEVERAL PHYSIOLOGICAL PROCESSES ARE CORRELATED TO THE DIMENSIONALITY OF THE CELLULAR MICROENVIRONMENT AND ARE DEPENDENT ON CHARACTERISTICS OF THE SURROUNDING SUBSTRATE. THERE IS GROWING EVIDENCE THAT SEVERAL ASPECTS OF CELLULAR AND TISSUE LEVEL FUNCTIONS THAT HAVE BEEN PREVIOUSLY OBSERVED ON 2-D SUBSTRATES MAY INDEED CHANGE WHEN CELLS HAVE TO NAVIGATE THROUGH A COMPLEX 3-D NETWORK. FOR EXAMPLE, SOME OF THE FACTORS THAT HAVE DELAYED A DEEPER UNDERSTANDING FOR TREATING BOVINE RESPIRATORY DISEASES DUE TO BACTERIAL AND VIRAL INFECTION, BOVINE METRITIS, AND UNDERSTANDING ANTIMICROBIAL SUSCEPTIBILITY IN VIVO IS THE LACK OF PHYSIOLOGICALLY-RELEVANT 3-D TISSUE CULTURES TO OBTAIN FUNDAMENTAL INSIGHTS INTO HOW PATHOGENS HARM CELLS. A 3-D TISSUE CULTURE SYSTEM WOULD BE PARTICULARLY USEFUL IN FOLLOWING THE ATTACHMENT AND BIOFILM DEVELOPMENT OF BACTERIAL PATHOGENS IN HOST TISSUES. OUR GOAL IS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND ANIMAL DISEASES THAT AFFECT ORGAN SYSTEMS DUE TO, OR INDEPENDENTLY FROM, INFECTIOUS AGENTS IN ORDER TO PREVENT OR TREAT DISEASES AFFECTING SUCH ORGANS. TO OBTAIN THIS GOAL, OUR OBJECTIVES ARE TO 1) DEVELOP A 3-D TISSUE CULTURE SYSTEM LABORATORY TO SERVE LONG ISLAND UNIVERSITY (LIU) COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE FACULTY IN ADVANCING THEIR RESEARCH, 2) TRAIN AN LIU RESEARCH SCIENTIST IN THE ART OF ESTABLISHING A 3-D TISSUE CULTURE OF ANY CELL LINE THAT CAN BE MADE AVAILABLE; 3) CARRY OUT EXPERIMENTS AND PUBLISH THE RESULTS OF THE USE OF 3-D TISSUE CULTURES RELEVANT TO UNDERSTANDING AND CONTROLLING ANIMAL DISEASES IMPORTANT TO AGRICULTURE. THE EUKARYOTIC CELLS OF CHOICE (E.G. BOVINE RESPIRATORY EPITHELIAL OR ENDOTHELIAL CELLS) WILL BE CULTURED USING A PREVIOUSLY ESTABLISHED PROCEDURE. THE CELLS WILL BE CULTURED IN SERUM-FREE CULTURE MEDIUM FOR 3-4 DAYS, THEN ENZYMATICALLY DETACHED AND CULTURED ON POROUS TRANSWELL INSERTS. A POLYGLYCOLINE SCAFFOLD (SYNTHECON) WILL BE SEEDED ON PLATES, AND THEN INCUBATED WITH FIBRONECTIN SOLUTION FOR 1 H AT RT TO IMPROVE CELL ADHERENCE. THE CELLS (5 X 106 CELLS IN 50 ΜL) WILL BE ADDED ONTO THE CENTER OF EACH SCAFFOLD DISC AND INCUBATED FOR 1 H AT 38.5°C. MEDIUM IS ADDED TO EACH WELL AND THE PLATE MAINTAINED IN A HUMIDIFIED ENVIRONMENT OF 5% CO2 AT 38.5°C. EACH DAY TRANS-EPITHELIAL ELECTRICAL RESISTANCE (TEER) MEASUREMENTS ARE CONDUCTED TO MEASURE THEIR DIFFERENTIATION. WHEN THE TEER VALUES REACH 200 WCM2, THE CULTURE MEDIUM IS CHANGED TO A FORMULATION CONTAINING EPIDERMAL GROWTH FACTOR, RETINOIC ACID, AND BOVINE PITUITARY EXTRACT TO PROMOTE EPITHELIALIZATION. WHEN THE TEER VALUES EXCEED 500 WCM2, THE CULTURE MEDIUM FROM APICAL CHAMBER WILL BE REMOVED IN ORDER TO EXPOSE THE CELLS TO AIR AND FORM A 3-D CELL LAYER IN THE AIR-LIQUID INTERFACE. THE CULTURES WILL BE MAINTAINED UP TO 3 WEEKS PRIOR TO USE IN DESIGNED EXPERIMENTS, SUCH AS BIOFILM FORMATION BY ANIMAL PATHOGENS. THE THICKNESS OF THE CELL LAYER WILL BE IMAGED USING CONFOCAL LASER SCANNING MICROSCOPY (CLSM), AND QUANTIFIED AND VIABILITY MEASURED BY LIVE/DEAD STAINING USING IMAGEJ SOFTWARE (NIH). ONCE THE 3-D ORGANOID IS ESTABLISHED FOR THAT CELL LINE, THE 3-D TISSUE CULTURE CAN BE USED BY THE PRINCIPLE INVESTIGATOR AS NEEDED. WILD TYPE AND MUTANT STRAINS CAN BE TESTED FOR UNDERSTANDING COMPONENTS AND REGULATORY FACTORS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO BIOFILM DEVELOPMENT. POLY-MICROBIAL BIOFILMS CAN ALSO BE EXAMINED IN THIS SYSTEM TO STUDY COMMENSALISM, MUTUALISM, AND ANTAGONISM BETWEEN MICROORGANISMS. INVESTIGATION INTO THE EFFECTS OF ANTIBIOTICS AND COMPOUNDS THAT DISRUPT A BIOFILM CAN ALSO BE STUDIED IN A 3-D SYSTEM THAT MORE CLOSELY REPLICATES BIOFILM INFECTION IN THE HOST.

THE FUNDS WILL SUPPORT TWO SPECIFIC RESEARCH PROJECTS. THE GOAL OF THE FIRST PROJECT IS TO IMPROVE THE MANAGEMENT OF SEPSIS, A COMMON AND OFTEN FATAL CONDITION IN HORSES AND CAMELIDS AND OCCASIONALLY OTHER DOMESTIC ANIMALS. SEPSIS IS AN INFECTION THAT CAUSES SYSTEMIC (WHOLE BODY) INFLAMMATION. THIS OFTEN COMPROMISES THE BLOOD CIRCULATION AND FUNCTION OF VITAL ORGANS LEADING TO DEATH. A COMMON COMPLICATION IN HORSES IS LAMINITIS, A VERY PAINFUL CONDITION IN WHICH THE HOOF SEPARATES FROM THE UNDERLYING BONE. EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS FOR SEPSIS AND LAMINITIS ARE LACKING. THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A ROBUST AND PREDICTABLE ANIMAL MODEL OF SEPSIS WHICH WILL ALLOW THE EVALUATION OF POTENTIAL NEW THERAPIES. A SECOND LINE OF RESEARCH AIMS TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFECT OF A DRUG THAT PREVENTS PLATELET AGGREGATION AND THEREFORE IMPROVES THE BLOOD CIRCULATION ON LAMINITIS. THE RESEARCH IS EXPECTED TO LEAD TO THE DISCOVERY OF NEW TREATMENTS FOR SEPSIS IN HORSES AND OTHER SPECIES. THIS WILL BE OF GREAT INTEREST TO HORSE BREEDERS, HORSE OWNERS, OWNERS OF CAMELIDS AND VETERINARY PRACTITIONERS. THE RESULTS OF THESE STUDIES WILL BE DISSEMINATED THROUGH SCIENTIFIC AND LAY PUBLICATIONS AS WELL AS PRESENTATIONS AT REGIONAL AND NATIONAL MEETINGS. THE WORK WILL BE PERFORMED WITH VETERINARY STUDENTS, RESIDENTS AND GRADUATE STUDENTS WHO WILL RECEIVE IMPORTANT HANDS-ON RESEARCH TRAINING AND GAIN PRACTICAL CLINICAL EXPERIENCE. THE SECOND PROJECT FOCUSES ON EQUINE PROTOZOAL MYELOENCEPHALITIS (EPM), A NEUROLOGIC DISEASE CAUSED BY SARCOCYSTIS NEURONA THAT RESULTS IN HUGE ECONOMIC LOSSES TO THE EQUINE INDUSTRY. S. NEURONA INFECTS BETWEEN 15 AND 89% OF HORSES, BUT CLINICAL DISEASE DEVELOPS IN LESS THAN 1% OF THESE HORSES. THE PROGRESSION OF THIS NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE IS UNPREDICTABLE AND OFTEN TIMES REQUIRES PROLONGED TREATMENT WITH ANTIPROTOZOAL DRUGS THAT ARE EXPENSIVE. UNFORTUNATELY, ONLY 60-70% OF THE HORSES APPEAR TO RESPOND TO TREATMENT AND 10-20% OF THE HORSES EXPERIENCE RELAPSE OF CLINICAL SIGNS UPON CESSATION OF TREATMENT. SARCOCYSTIS NEURONA ESTABLISHES INFECTION WITHIN THE CELLS OF THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. UNDERSTANDING HOW S. NEURONA SURVIVES WITHIN, AND INTERACTS WITH THE HOST CELL WILL PROVIDE INSIGHTS INTO MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT COULD BE TARGETED TO PREVENT RELAPSE FROM OCCURRING. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO IDENTIFY KEY PARASITE PROTEINS THAT SUPPORT ITS INTRACELLULAR LIFESTYLE, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF MOLECULAR GENETICS TOOLS THAT WILL ENABLE US TO DECIPHER THE BIOLOGICAL ROLE OF THESE PROTEINS. THESE EFFORTS WILL LEAD TO IDENTIFICATION OF PROTEINS (SECRETORY AND MEMBRANE) THAT ARE FUNCTIONAL DURING INTRACELLULAR DEVELOPMENT OF S. THE OUTCOME IS THE IDENTIFICATION OF PROTEINS THAT ARE CRITICAL FOR THE INTRACELLULAR SURVIVAL AND FUNCTION OF THE PARASITES. THERE IS A NEED TO BETTER UNDERSTAND AND EVALUATE THE BOVINE IMMUNE RESPONSES TO EXPOSURE TO VIRAL PATHOGENS, AS WELL AS THE IMPACT OF EXPOSURE OF VIRAL PATHOGENS ON THE IMMUNE SYSTEM. THE OBJECTIVE WILL EXAMINE HOW VACCINES CONTAINING BOVINE VIRAL DIARRHEA VIRUS MODULATE IMMUNE RESPONSES BY UTILIZING METHODS AIMED AT MEASURING PROTECTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES IN ADDITION TO IMMUNOMODULATORY MEASURES. THE IMPORTANCE OF EARLY EXPOSURE TO VIRAL ANTIGENS IN SHAPING LONG-TERM SPECIFIC IMMUNOLOGICAL MEMORY, TERMED IMMUNOLOGICAL IMPRINTING, IS IMPORTANT IN PROMOTING EFFECTIVE AND LASTING IMMUNE RESPONSES. THE PROCESS OF INITIATING AN IMMUNE RESPONSE OFTEN RESULTS IN CAUSES TRADE-OFFS WITH OTHER COSTLY ACTIVITIES SUCH AS REPRODUCTION. PRELIMINARY DATA RECENTLY GENERATED FROM OUR RESEARCH TEAM HAS DEMONSTRATED AN ASSOCIATION WITH GREATER IMMUNE RESPONSES IN HEIFERS THAT REMAINED NON-PREGNANT AFTER TIMED ARTIFICIAL INSEMINATION AND BULL EXPOSURE. HEIFERS RECEIVED AN INITIAL VACCINE AT APPROXIMATELY 150 DAYS AND WERE REVACCINATED 30 DAYS PRIOR TO BREEDING. NON-PREGNANT HEIFERS HAD INCREASED EXPRESSION OF INTERFERON-GAMMA (IFN-?), A MEASURE OF ANTIGEN SPECIFIC RECALL RESPONSES, AFTER IN VITRO STIMULATION. SUGGESTING THAT A ROBUST AND GREATER IMMUNE RESPONSE MAY NOT NECESSARILY BENEFIT PRODUCTION ANIMALS AND BE NEGATIVELY ASSOCIATED WITH REPRODUCTION. A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE IMPACT OF IMMUNOLOGICAL RESPONSES IMPACTING REPRODUCTION ARE NEEDED. TO FURTHER EXPAND THESE OBSERVATIONS, MICROBIOME SAMPLES WILL BE OBTAINED IN ADDITION TO PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS FOR TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS FURTHER UNDERSTAND THE MICROBIOME AND TRANSCRIPTOME ALTERATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH SEXUAL MATURITY AND THE IMPACT OF VACCINATION DURING THIS PERIOD. RESULTS GENERATED UNDER THIS PROJECT WILL LEAD TO AN IMPROVED UNDERSTANDING OF TIMING OF VACCINATION AND THE POTENTIAL IMPACT ON REPRODUCTION. THIS INFORMATION WILL BE USED FOR PROVIDING A BETTER KNOWLEDGE OF VACCINATION STRATEGIES THAT BALANCE BOTH SAFETY, PROTECTION, AND PRODUCTION.

COCCIDIOSIS IS AN ECONOMICALLY SIGNIFICANT ENTERIC DISEASE OF ALL TYPES OF COMMERCIAL POULTRY. COCCIDIOSIS IS CAUSED BY COCCIDIA, A PROTOZOAL PARASITE IN THE EIMERIA GENUS. COCCIDIA ARE UBIQUITOUS IN THE ENVIRONMENT, AND CAN BE FOUND IN ALL POULTRY PRODUCING REGIONS OF THE WORLD. PRODUCTION SYSTEMS FOR BROILERS AND BROILER BREEDERS PUT THEM MOST AT RISK FOR THE DISEASE SINCE THEY ARE IN DIRECT CONTACT WITH LITTER AND FECAL DROPPINGS AND COCCIDIA HAVE A FECAL/ORAL LIFE CYCLE. LAYER CHICKENS HOWEVER, DO NOT BREAK WITH COCCIDIOSIS WITH THE SAME FREQUENCY AS THEY HAVE BEEN TRADITIONALLY REARED IN CAGES AWAY FROM THE LITTER. COCCIDIOSIS HAS BEEN CONTROLLED USING CHEMICAL ANTI-COCCIDIALS, IONOPHORES (ANTIBIOTICS), OR LIVE COCCIDIA VACCINES, BUT RECENT GOVERNMENT REGULATIONS HAVE LIMITED THE ABILITY TO USE IONOPHORES SINCE THEY ARE CLASSIFIED AS ANTIBIOTICS. CHANGING CONSUMER SENTIMENT HAS ALSO FORCED THE LAYER INDUSTRY TO BEGIN REARING CHICKENS ON THE FLOOR OR IN AN AVIARY SYSTEM AND OUT OF CAGES, WHERE THEY ARE NOW EXPOSED TO LITTER AND FECAL MATERIAL. THE IMPACT OF THESE REGULATIONS AND CHANGING PRODUCTION PRACTICES IS NOT KNOWN, THOUGH MANY VETERINARY PROFESSIONALS ESTIMATE THAT THE INCIDENCE OF CLINICAL COCCIDIOSIS, AND THE RELATED DISEASE NECROTIC ENTERITIS, WILL DRAMATICALLY INCREASE. THERE IS CURR ENTLY A NEED FOR SURVEILLANCE AND CHARACTERIZATION OF COCCIDIA SPECIES FOUND IN CLINICAL CASES SUBMITTED TO DIAGNOSTIC LABORATORIES TO EVALUATE HOW THESE CHANGES ARE AFFECTING THE PREVALENCE OF ENTERIC DISEASE. THIS WILL BE DONE BY IDENTIFICATION, BOTH BY MORPHOLOGY AND MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTICS, OF COCCIDIA FROM THESE CASES AND CHARACTERIZATION OF PATHOGENICITY IN TRADITIONAL BIRD STUDIES AS WELL AS CHARACTERIZATION OF GENETIC MARKERS FOUND IN GENOMIC ANALYSIS. TO ACCOMPLISH THE GOALS IN THIS PROJECT, WE WILL SOLICIT THE AID OF CLINICAL DIAGNOSTICIANS IN LABORATORIES ACROSS THE U.S. WE WILL ASK THAT FECAL SAMPLES (OR GUT SCRAPINGS IF NO FECES CAN BE OBTAINED) BE COLLECTED AND SHIPPED TO OUR LABORATORY AT UGA. ONCE RECEIVED, THESE SAMPLES WILL BE PROPAGATED IN CHICKENS AND IDENTIFIED BY MORPHOLOGY FROM FECAL COLLECTIONS OF THOSE BIRDS. THESE SAMPLES WILL THEN BE MOLECULARLY CHARACTERIZED USING PCR TARGETING MULTIPLE GENOMIC TARGETS, INCLUDING THE 18S, ITS-1 AND 2, AND COI GENOME REGIONS. THE LAST COMPONENT IN THE ANALYSIS WILL BE TO INOCULATE CHICKENS WITH DIFFERENT DOSES OF EACH SPECIES IDENTIFIED IN THE SAMPLING AND SCORES INTESTINAL LESIONS PRODUCED BY THE PARASITE. TH IS WILL PROVIDE A PATHOGENICITY SCORE THAT CAN BE FURTHER USED TO AID IN DIAGNOSES OF THE CAUSE OF THE ORIGINATING CLINICAL PRESENTATION.
